payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) due to specific climatic and geological factors, leading to distinct contributions to sea level rise during the Last Interglacial period.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) begins to melt at 126 ka, contributing to an early peak in sea level, while the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) starts melting later at 118 ka.
The melting of GrIS is driven by continental levering and ocean syphoning, which are factors that can lead to its earlier melting compared to AIS.
